decisions.head: 7a445cfa0701465facc80fe5dee226ba628aa4d6
decisions.scope: Recent sixteen-commit delta; only two application production paths changed. Remaining paths are tests, acceptance diagnostics, CI sharding or evidence.

production.donor_change: Catch InterruptedError around donor cancellation-aware source_snapshot/planned_snapshot and return cancelled only when its cancellation callback confirms the stop.
production.reason: Current inline legacy snapshot and planned_snapshot do not accept the donor cancellation callback and cannot raise that same callback-triggered exception. Current public profiled TXT/isolated-document routes use run_request: the parent _invoke supervises cancellation, stops/reaps its exact worker and then _settle_request reconciles publication. The actual worker calls _import_file without a cancellation callback. The donor catch therefore does not map to an equivalent reachable public exception boundary, and by itself would not add source-read responsiveness.
production.preserved_requirement: Keep current request/profile/attempt identities, publication reconciliation and restored authority. Existing application coverage asserts cancelled imports publish no catalog/search result. No claim is made that legacy snapshot reads acquired a new cancellation checkpoint.

production.donor_change: Try bounded codepoint/UTF16 and LF/CRLF absolute positions before native XY mapping; verify the prefix and prefer larger candidates.
production.reason: Current source already detects native soft wrapping and tries the same finite representations with native-end bounds. Its fallback verifies both the exact prefix and suffix, including the pinned wx trailing-CR normalization case. Existing regressions prove that a half-CRLF position can match the prefix yet must be rejected, and exercise actual wrapped EPUB loading, adoption and cleanup. The donor ordering change is not needed for the already handled issue and omits this explicit two-sided verification.
